_meta.description: Curated triage evaluation scenarios for MediAgent AI's run_triage_pipeline().
schema_notes: Each case is assembled into the exact multi-line 'symptoms' string app.py builds, and a 'Age: X, Gender: Y' patient_context string, so the pipeline is exercised the same way the real UI exercises it.

expected_severity / expected_departments / expected_urgency_[min|max] reflect the CLINICALLY correct answer, independent of whether the current deterministic guardrail layer (agents/pipeline.py: apply_triage_guardrails) actually produces it.

category 'guardrail_probe' cases exist specifically to test known guardrail edge cases (e.g. Critical cases worded without the hardcoded red-flag substrings, which Rule 4 will incorrectly downgrade to Moderate; or chest-pain-without-red-flag-phrase cases where Rule 2 can leave severity=Critical paired with department=Cardiology and urgency clamped to 6-8).
category 'invalid' cases are gibberish/non-medical input meant to test the Intake Agent's INVALID path, not the triage logic.

Mental-health cases are deliberately limited to non-crisis presentations (mild anxiety, sleep disruption, stress) -- crisis/self-harm risk triage is out of scope for this synthetic set and should be handled by a dedicated, specialist-reviewed protocol, not a general LLM triage pipeline.

cases.description: Sudden severe difficulty breathing, gasping for air, lips look bluish
cases.notes: Contains guardrail red-flag phrase 'difficulty breathing' -> should hit Rule 1 deterministically.

cases.description: Patient lost consciousness for about 30 seconds after standing up, now confused
cases.notes: Contains 'loss of consciousness' red-flag phrase.

cases.description: Whole body shaking, unresponsive for about a minute, this was a seizure witnessed by family
cases.notes: Contains 'seizure' red-flag phrase.

cases.description: Face drooping on one side, slurred speech, right arm feels weak, started 20 minutes ago
cases.notes: Contains 'face drooping' and 'slurred speech' red-flag phrases (classic FAST stroke signs).

cases.description: Vomiting blood, bright red, has happened twice in the last hour
cases.notes: Contains 'vomiting blood' red-flag phrase.

cases.description: Took a new antibiotic, now has a severe allergic reaction with swelling of the lips and throat tightness
cases.notes: Contains 'severe allergic reaction' red-flag phrase.

cases.description: Deep cut from a saw, heavy bleeding that soaked through two towels already
cases.notes: Contains 'heavy bleeding' red-flag phrase.

cases.description: Crushing chest pain that started while climbing stairs, pain radiates to the jaw, feeling nauseous and sweaty
cases.notes: Contains 'crushing chest pain' red-flag phrase -> Rule 1 should fire before the Cardiology rule, keeping this out of ER-101's ambiguity.

cases.description: Was stung by a bee, now cannot breathe properly and throat feels like it's closing
cases.notes: Contains 'cannot breathe' red-flag phrase.

cases.description: Coughing up blood, bright red streaks, has happened three times today along with chest discomfort
cases.notes: Contains 'coughing blood' red-flag phrase.

cases.description: Sudden crushing pressure in the center of the chest spreading to the left shoulder, breaking out in a cold sweat, feels like an elephant is sitting on my chest
cases.notes: GUARDRAIL PROBE: classic ACS presentation but phrased without 'chest pressure' verbatim and without any Rule-1 substring. If the LLM correctly says Critical, Rule 2 (cardiology_signals matches 'chest') may fire first and route to Cardiology with urgency clamped 6-8 instead of Emergency/9-10 -- flag as an internal-consistency failure, not a clinical-labeling failure.

cases.description: Sudden worst headache of my life, vision is blurry in one eye and I feel very confused about where I am
cases.notes: GUARDRAIL PROBE: thunderclap headache + confusion is a stroke/hemorrhage red flag clinically, but doesn't match any literal Rule-1 substring ('confused' != 'new severe confusion' wording used in the prompt). Tests whether the LLM's own judgement survives Rule 4's blanket Critical-downgrade when no hardcoded phrase is present.

cases.description: Started a new antibiotic an hour ago, now covered in hives with the throat feeling tight and swallowing is getting harder
cases.notes: GUARDRAIL PROBE: early anaphylaxis described without the exact phrase 'severe allergic reaction' or 'anaphylaxis' -> tests whether Rule 4 downgrades a correct LLM Critical call.

cases.description: Calf suddenly swollen, hot, and painful after a long flight yesterday, and now feeling short of breath climbing stairs
cases.notes: GUARDRAIL PROBE: classic DVT + possible pulmonary embolism picture ('short of breath' rather than the hardcoded 'difficulty breathing'/'shortness of breath' phrase is not in the red-flag list at all) -> good test of whether wording sensitivity causes a missed emergency.

cases.description: Sudden severe stabbing pain in the lower right abdomen, worse when pressing and releasing, fever, vomiting since this morning
cases.notes: GUARDRAIL PROBE: textbook appendicitis (surgical emergency) but matches none of the hardcoded red-flag substrings -> tests whether non-cardiac, non-respiratory surgical emergencies get silently downgraded to Moderate/General Medicine by Rule 4.

cases.description: Occasional chest tightness for the past two days, comes and goes, no shortness of breath, happens mostly when stressed
cases.notes: Mild intermittent chest tightness without red flags should route to Cardiology per Rule 2 without being escalated to Critical.

cases.description: Heart palpitations and a fluttering feeling in the chest for the last hour, no pain, no dizziness
cases.notes: Palpitations without red flags -> Cardiology, Moderate.

cases.description: Irregular heartbeat noticed on and off for a week, feels like skipped beats, otherwise feeling fine
cases.notes: Chronic irregular heartbeat, no acute red flags -> Cardiology, Moderate.

cases.description: Mild chest discomfort after eating a large spicy meal, feels like heartburn, has happened before
cases.notes: Ambiguous chest-discomfort-vs-reflux case. 'chest discomfort' will trigger the Cardiology guardrail signal regardless of the more likely GI cause -- included to test whether the system over-routes benign reflux-type chest discomfort to Cardiology.

cases.description: Rapid heartbeat after drinking several energy drinks this afternoon, feels jittery, no chest pain
cases.notes: Stimulant-induced tachycardia, no red flags -> Cardiology, Moderate.

cases.description: Persistent dry cough for the past three weeks, gets worse at night, no fever
cases.notes: Persistent cough >3 weeks warrants Pulmonology per the routing rules.

cases.description: Known asthma, using rescue inhaler more often than usual this week, mild wheezing but no severe breathing difficulty
cases.notes: Worsening asthma control without acute severe distress -> Pulmonology, Moderate.

cases.description: Diagnosed with COPD, more breathless than usual with daily activities over the last two weeks
cases.notes: Chronic lung disease with gradual worsening -> Pulmonology, Moderate.

cases.description: Chronic cough for over a month that started after a cold, coughing up clear mucus, no blood, no fever now
cases.notes: Chronic post-viral cough -> Pulmonology per routing rules.

cases.description: Runny nose, mild sore throat, and a slight cough for the last two days, feeling generally tired
cases.notes: Uncomplicated common cold -> Mild, General Medicine.

cases.description: Low-grade fever and body aches since yesterday, no other symptoms, resting at home
cases.notes: Fever/body aches without emergency red flags -> Mild-to-low-Moderate, General Medicine per the specific fever guidance.

cases.description: Feeling fatigued and a bit weak for the past two days, mild headache, otherwise okay
cases.notes: Nonspecific fatigue/mild headache -> Mild, General Medicine.

cases.description: Mild sore throat and slight cough for one day, no fever, no difficulty swallowing
cases.notes: Uncomplicated sore throat, could reasonably land in either General Medicine or ENT.

cases.description: High fever of 103F for the last day, chills, feeling very weak and unable to keep fluids down
cases.notes: High fever + dehydration risk (unable to keep fluids down) -> Moderate per the specific fever guidance, still General Medicine, not Critical.

cases.description: Cold symptoms for a week that seem to be getting worse instead of better, now with a persistent fever
cases.notes: Worsening cold with persistent fever -> Moderate per the cold/cough guidance, General Medicine (should not go to Pulmonology).

cases.description: Mild nausea and a couple episodes of loose stool since this morning, no blood, no severe pain
cases.notes: Short-duration mild GI upset without red flags -> Mild, General Medicine is an acceptable first point of care.

cases.description: Repeated vomiting more than 6 times today, unable to keep any food or water down, feeling dizzy when standing
cases.notes: Significant vomiting with dehydration risk -> Moderate, Gastroenterology.

cases.description: Blood noticed in stool twice this week, otherwise feeling okay, mild intermittent abdominal discomfort
cases.notes: Blood in stool warrants Moderate + Gastroenterology per the specific GI guidance (not automatically Critical without other red flags).

cases.description: Recurrent stomach pain after meals for the past two weeks, bloating, occasional heartburn
cases.notes: Persistent recurrent GI symptoms -> Gastroenterology per routing rules.

cases.description: Ate at a roadside stall yesterday, now believes it is food poisoning with mild stomach cramps and one episode of diarrhea
cases.notes: Tests that the pipeline does not treat the patient's self-diagnosed 'food poisoning' as confirmed and does not exaggerate urgency for mild, short-duration symptoms.

cases.description: Severe sudden abdominal pain that won't go away, worse when moving, feels rigid to the touch, feeling feverish
cases.notes: GUARDRAIL PROBE: rigid, severe, acute abdomen is a surgical emergency (possible perforation/peritonitis) but matches no hardcoded red-flag substring -> another test of Rule 4's blind spot for non-cardiopulmonary emergencies.

cases.description: Recurring migraines for years, today's episode is typical of past migraines, sensitivity to light, no new symptoms
cases.notes: Typical migraine matching known pattern, no new focal deficits -> Moderate, not Critical despite high pain score.

cases.description: Numbness and tingling in the fingers of one hand for the past three days, no weakness, no head symptoms
cases.notes: Gradual, isolated peripheral numbness in a diabetic (possible neuropathy) -> Moderate, not an acute stroke picture.

cases.description: New onset of one-sided arm and leg weakness that started 15 minutes ago while watching TV, also has trouble finding words
cases.notes: GUARDRAIL PROBE: sudden focal weakness + word-finding difficulty is a stroke until proven otherwise, but uses 'weakness'/'trouble finding words' rather than the hardcoded 'sudden weakness'/'slurred speech' phrasing exactly -> tests phrase-sensitivity of Rule 1.

cases.description: Dull headache on and off for two days, mild, worse with stress, no vision changes or other symptoms
cases.notes: Classic tension headache, no red flags -> Mild.

cases.description: Twisted ankle playing football yesterday, swollen and painful to walk on, can bear a little weight
cases.notes: Acute ankle sprain, weight-bearing -> Moderate, Orthopedics.

cases.description: Chronic lower back pain for months, flared up after lifting a heavy box two days ago, no leg weakness or numbness
cases.notes: Mechanical back pain flare without neuro red flags -> Mild-to-low-Moderate.

cases.description: Fell on an outstretched hand while cycling, wrist is swollen, deformed-looking, and very painful to move
cases.notes: Likely fracture given visible deformity -> prompt (same-day) Orthopedics evaluation, Moderate-to-high-urgency but not a Critical/Emergency case in isolation.

cases.description: Itchy red rash on both forearms for three days, mild, no swelling of face or throat, tried an over-the-counter cream with no improvement
cases.notes: Uncomplicated skin rash without systemic or allergic emergency signs -> Mild.

cases.description: A mole on the back has changed shape and color over the last two months, no pain
cases.notes: Changing mole warrants prompt Dermatology evaluation -> Moderate.

cases.description: Ear pain and a feeling of fullness for two days, mild hearing reduction on that side, no fever
cases.notes: Likely otitis media in a child -> Mild-to-low-Moderate, ENT or Pediatrics both reasonable.

cases.description: Severe sore throat and difficulty swallowing even liquids for the past day, voice sounds muffled
cases.notes: Difficulty swallowing with muffled voice raises concern for peritonsillar abscess -> prompt ENT evaluation, Moderate.

cases.description: Red, itchy, watery eyes for two days, mild discharge, no vision changes or pain
cases.notes: Likely conjunctivitis/allergic eyes -> Mild.

cases.description: Sudden loss of vision in one eye like a curtain coming down, no pain, started an hour ago
cases.notes: GUARDRAIL PROBE: sudden painless vision loss is a time-critical ophthalmological/vascular emergency (e.g. retinal artery occlusion) but matches none of the hardcoded red-flag substrings -> tests whether non-cardiopulmonary, non-neuro-worded emergencies are missed entirely.

cases.description: Feeling more anxious than usual for the past two weeks, trouble falling asleep, no thoughts of self-harm, work has been stressful
cases.notes: Non-crisis mild anxiety/insomnia -> Mild-to-low-Moderate, Psychiatry or General Medicine referral, routine (not urgent) evaluation.

cases.description: Low mood and low energy for the past month, still going to work and eating normally, wants to talk to someone
cases.notes: Persistent low mood affecting functioning warrants a prompt, non-emergency Psychiatry referral -> Moderate.

cases.description: 3-year-old with fever of 101F for one day, still playful and drinking fluids, mild runny nose
cases.notes: Well-appearing febrile toddler with a viral picture -> Mild-to-low-Moderate, Pediatrics.

cases.description: 6-month-old baby has had a fever of 102F for the last 6 hours, unusually fussy and not feeding well
cases.notes: Fever in a young infant (<1 year) with poor feeding warrants prompt pediatric evaluation given higher baseline risk in infants -> Moderate-to-high-urgency.

cases.description: Blood sugar readings have been consistently high for the past week despite taking medication as prescribed, feeling more thirsty than usual
cases.notes: Poor glycemic control trend -> prompt Endocrinology follow-up, Moderate.

cases.description: Unexplained weight loss and feeling unusually hot and sweaty for the past month, heart racing at times
cases.notes: Possible hyperthyroidism picture, gradual onset, no acute red flags -> Moderate.

cases.description: 8 weeks pregnant with mild spotting today, no cramping, no heavy bleeding
cases.notes: Any bleeding in early pregnancy warrants prompt OB evaluation even without severe pain -> Moderate.

cases.description: Painful and heavier than usual periods for the last two cycles, otherwise healthy
cases.notes: Non-acute gynecological complaint -> Mild-to-low-Moderate, routine OB/Gyn follow-up.

cases.description: asdkjh aksjdh qwerty 12345 blah blah
cases.notes: Gibberish input -> Intake Agent should return INVALID, run_triage_pipeline should return valid=False.

cases.description: bad
cases.notes: Single vague word, too unspecific to triage -> should be flagged INVALID.

cases.description: what is the weather like today in Bhopal
cases.notes: Non-medical input -> should be flagged INVALID, not triaged.
